subject: Concurrency & rate limits — follow-up and proposed quota
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmecorp.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-20T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap — concurrency & streaming requirements

Hi Tom — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups so we have alignment on performance/SLO requirements before Laura drafts the quota proposal: 

Summary of what I heard from the call:
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 200ms for non-streaming inference; streaming responses acceptable with partial tokens emitted within 150ms for first token.
- Throughput: steady-state ~300 req/s across the service, with anticipated sustained peaks up to ~600 req/s during batch jobs.
- Concurrency: plan to make parallel requests from many users — expect ~120 concurrent long-lived connections during business hours, with peak bursts to ~500 concurrent requests for 30–90s during product launches.
- Connection model: prefer HTTP/2 or persistent HTTP/1.1 keep-alive; wants ability to reuse connections (connection pooling) from our side.
- Tokenization/load per request: average payload results in ~1200 tokens generated per call (varies by prompt).

Items I promised to follow up on:
1) Laura will send a proposed concurrency/rate-limit profile and suggested quota numbers we think will meet your SLOs.
2) We’ll include a brief pilot plan (canary window, monitoring hooks, rollback) and the impact on committed cost.
3) Please share the best SRE contact for test coordination + any firewall/allowlist IPs if you need private connectivity.

Next steps:
- Laura: can you send the draft quota/proposal by EOD Tuesday?
- Tom: please confirm your SRE contact and whether HTTP/2 is required or optional.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Markus on the billing/contract side once we have the proposed quotas.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0192
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2027-06-21T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — concurrency & streaming requirements

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirmation and a couple of clarifications from our side: 

- Latency: p95 <= 200ms is the target for non-streaming endpoints. For streaming, first-byte within 150ms is ideal but we can accept up to 300ms during heavy load.
- Throughput/concurrency: our internal telemetry suggests baseline traffic will be ~250 req/s, rising to 500–600 req/s for sustained periods (~10–30 minutes) during peak operations. We’re more concerned about concurrent inflight requests during releases — those can spike to ~700 for short windows.
- Connection pooling: HTTP/2 would be preferred (multiplexing helps our client), but if unavailable we can use long-lived HTTP/1.1 connections with keep-alive and a pool size of ~50 per service instance.

SRE contact for coordination is me + sre@acmecorp.com. We can do a tech sync next week. Also want to understand what Redwood’s default hosted rate limits are and how a dedicated quota would differ (both capacity and pricing).

Tom
Tom Reynolds
Head of Product Ops, Acme Robotics
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-22T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — concurrency & streaming requirements

Tom — thanks, this is helpful. I put together a proposed profile and a short explanation of how we recommend handling concurrency and rate limits to meet your SLOs. Attached: redwood-concurrency-proposal-ACME.pdf (contains numbers, cost estimate, and pilot plan). Highlights below: 

Proposed quota (Dedicated / Reserved capacity recommendation):
- Reserved concurrency tokens: 500 concurrent inference slots for ACME (guaranteed).
- Burst capacity: allow bursts up to 800 concurrent requests for up to 120s (best-effort) to handle release spikes.
- RPS target: baseline 600 req/s sustained, with headroom to 1,200 req/s for short bursts (token-bucket smoothing).
- Streaming concurrency: support for 300 simultaneous streaming sessions (we separate streaming slots from short non-streaming inference slots to avoid head-of-line issues).
- Connection model: HTTP/2 supported on Dedicated + Private deployments. For Hosted, we recommend HTTP/2 where possible; otherwise keep-alive pools.

How this maps to SLOs:
- The reserved concurrency ensures p95 latency headroom for the 200ms target on average payloads (1200 tokens).
- Burst buffer + autoscale policy reduces dropped requests during launch spikes; we recommend a canary window (10% traffic) for 48 hours before full cutover.

Redwood’s typical hosted defaults (for context):
- Hosted API default: 60 req/s and 20 concurrent streams per account (this is conservative for self-serve).
- Dedicated: negotiated per-deal; numbers above reflect a Dedicated/reserved configuration.

Pilot plan (summary):
1) 2-week technical pilot on Dedicated pool with reserved concurrency 200 -> verify p95 under realistic load.
2) If pilot passes, expand reserved concurrency to 500 and enable burst 800 for 14 days of observation.
3) Telemetry: we'll enable per-route latency and token-level cost dashboards + a sample of request/response traces for root-cause.

Cost/contract notes:
- Laura: preliminary pricing for the Dedicated profile is in the attached PDF. Markus, can you confirm pricing cadence and any one-off setup fees?

Let us know if you want more aggressive reserved bursts or a different canary plan. Happy to hop on a technical call with SREs next week.

—
Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmecorp.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap — concurrency & streaming requirements

Laura/Marissa — appreciate the detailed proposal and the attached numbers. A few quick asks before we lock the pilot: 

1) Pricing impact: can Markus provide an estimate of monthly committed cost for the 500-reserved / 800-burst profile vs the 200-reserved pilot? We need a ballpark for internal approvals.
2) SLA: would Redwood provide an SLA for p95 latency under the reserved capacity profile? If so, what are the remedies for missed SLOs?
3) Pilot start: we’d like to begin the pilot July 6th. Are you able to provision trial capacity and a canary path starting that week?

We’re happy to do a short tech sync with Laura + your ops person (Markus?) on July 1st to finalize test scenarios and allowlist requirements.

Tom
